difficultyRationale: List has two remove methods and the argument type decides which one runs. Mixing up removal by index with removal by element is a very common mistake.
prompt:
What is printed by this program?

```java
{{snippet}}
```
explanation: remove(1) with an int argument calls remove(int index) and removes the element at index 1, which is 20, leaving [10, 30, 1]. remove(Integer.valueOf(1)) calls remove(Object) and removes the first element equal to 1, leaving [10, 30].

options.explanation: The first call removes by index (20), the second removes by value (the trailing 1).
This would result if remove(1) removed the value 1. An int argument selects remove(int index), so the element at index 1 is removed instead.
This is the list after only the first call. The second call removes the element equal to 1.
Neither call removes the first element. One removes index 1 and the other removes the value 1.
